newsitem.title: NIGERIA: NIGERIA COCOA GROUP SEES '97 CROP UP 10-20 PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: NIGERIA COCOA GROUP SEES '97 CROP UP 10-20 PERCENT.

text.p: Nigeria's cocoa association expects a rise in this year's crop of between 10 and 20 percent from last year when around 140,000 tonnes of beans were exported, the national news agency said on Monday.
Adeyanju Ojo, secretary general of the Cocoa Association of Nigeria, told the News Agency of Nigeria that once-abandoned farms were being brought back into production by peasant growers.
He also said warehousing conditions were improving, assisting storage before export.
Nigeria's cocoa exports have declined from 300,000 tonnes annually in the early 1970s when attention turned from agriculture to crude oil.
According to official data from the Federal Produce Inspection Agency, total exports for the 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) season reached 139,063 tonnes of beans.
Cumulative exports for the first eight months of the 1996/97 year totalled 126,324 tonnes, against 112,644 tonnes exported by the end of May 1996.
